name: Black
note: About 12.4% of deaths against 11% of the population over the whole war; but in 1965–1966 Black soldiers were roughly a fifth of Army combat deaths, and the Pentagon changed assignment patterns in 1967 to bring the share down. Project 100,000 (1966–1971) took 354,000 men below the normal standards, 41% of them Black, mostly into the infantry. In 1967 a draft-board study found 64% of eligible Black men were drafted against 31% of eligible whites, largely because of deferments the others could reach. Black officers were about 2% of the Army officer corps in 1968.
johnson: The Johnson years are the years this disproportion was largest, argued over (King, April 1967: “the cruel irony”), and then corrected in the field.
source: Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS), Vietnam Conflict Extract File, race field; US Census 1970; Guzmán 1969; Appy, Working-Class War (1993).
